scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Representatives must be data points: an outlier drags the mean, the medoid stays put

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: gray dots are the grid, blue dots the data; the red plus is the mean, the green ring the medoid (the data point with the smallest total distance to the others). The right panel adds an outlier $(9,2)$.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: Mean and medoid of six grid points

scene-u01-pnew1-80.name: text#80
scene-u01-pnew1-80.text: The medoid is not "the point nearest the mean" nor necessarily the median; it is the data point with the smallest total distance to the others.

scene-u01-pnew1-86.name: text#86
scene-u01-pnew1-86.text: The mean of grid points may be off the grid; the medoid never is.

scene-u01-pnew1-90.name: text#90
scene-u01-pnew1-90.text: An outlier pulls the mean noticeably but barely moves the medoid.

scene-u01-pnew1-94.name: text#94
scene-u01-pnew1-94.text: The mean has clear geometric and statistical meaning; the medoid may not.

scene-u01-pnew1-98.name: text#98
scene-u01-pnew1-98.text: Finding the best medoid set costs more than $k$-means.

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: PAM: examine every one-swap neighbor, take the smallest $\Delta J$; stop when all are $\ge0$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: green dots on the number line are medoids; the two bar groups show $\Delta J=J(\Theta_{ij})-J(\Theta)$ for the $8$ neighbors of each round, from $0$; green is the chosen swap.

scene-u01-pnew2-103.name: text#103
scene-u01-pnew2-103.text: In round $1$, $1\to9$ has the smallest $\Delta J=-18$; in round $2$ even the smallest is $+1$, so every swap raises $J$.

scene-u01-pnew2-117.name: text#117
scene-u01-pnew2-117.text: If the smallest $\Delta J<0$, swap and repeat

scene-u01-pnew2-121.name: text#121
scene-u01-pnew2-121.text: If the smallest $\Delta J\ge0$, stop at a local minimum

scene-u01-pnew2-125.name: text#125
scene-u01-pnew2-125.text: Each round checks $m(N-m)$ neighbors, each summing $N-m$ terms, so a round costs $O\bigl(m(N-m)^2\bigr)$; too slow for large data.

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Trade accuracy for speed by sampling: CLARA samples data, CLARANS samples neighbors

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the two cards on the left say what each samples; the right shows distance terms per round (step) for $N=1000$, $m=5$, on a log scale, comparing orders of magnitude only.

scene-u01-pnew3-13.name: text#13
scene-u01-pnew3-13.text: Draw a sample of size $N'$ from $X$ and run PAM on it

scene-u01-pnew3-15.name: text#15
scene-u01-pnew3-15.text: Repeat for $s$ samples and pick the best by $J$ on all of $X$

scene-u01-pnew3-23.name: text#23
scene-u01-pnew3-23.text: Runs on all of $X$ but checks only $q$ random neighbors per step

scene-u01-pnew3-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew3-25.text: Swap when one is better; if none of the $q$ is, treat it as a local minimum

scene-u01-pnew3-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew3-28.text: CLARANS usually clusters better; CLARA is sometimes much faster.

scene-u01-pnew3-56.name: text#56
scene-u01-pnew3-56.text: If CLARA's sample misses a small group, its medoids are biased.
